questions.question_text:
For this question, use classical categorical logic: universal statements carry no existential import; ‘some’ asserts existence; and ‘only a few X are Y’ means both that some X are Y and that some X are not Y. Possibility is assessed by whether at least one model satisfies it.
Statements:
1. All analysts are auditors.
2. No analysts are auditors.
Conclusions:
I. All analysts are auditors.
II. No analysts are auditors.
Which conclusion(s) logically follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation: All analysts are auditors; No analysts are auditors. Exhaustive three-set Venn-region checking leaves 15 nonempty models consistent with the statements. Conclusion I is true in every such model; conclusion II is true in every such model. Thus both conclusions follow.
questions.source: Original SSC Prep practice (not a PYQ); pattern references listed in chapter review report, accessed 2026-11-23.

questions.question_text:
Use classical categorical logic: universal statements carry no existential import; ‘some’ asserts existence; ‘only a few X are Y’ means some X are Y and some X are not Y. Test each possibility independently against the premises; the two conclusions may be true in different models.
Statements:
1. All analysts are auditors.
2. All clerks are auditors.
Conclusions:
I. It is possible that some analysts are clerks.
II. It is possible that no analysts are clerks.
Which conclusion(s) are possible?
questions.explanation: All analysts are auditors; All clerks are auditors. There are 31 nonempty Venn-region models satisfying the premises. An overlap model does exist; a disjoint model does exist. Since the conclusions are tested independently, both conclusions are possible.
questions.source: Original SSC Prep practice (not a PYQ); pattern references listed in chapter review report, accessed 2026-11-23.
